judgments.review_basis: No publicKeyMultibase/secretKeyMultibase header scheme is defined; DIDP-01 explicitly emits JWK and not Multikey. Raw registry key encodings are not new Multikey headers. [10 §6; 11 §§2–3]
No alternative representation-level extensibility mechanism is specified. The resolution sage metadata and A2A AgentExtension have different object scopes. [10 §§1,3,6; A2AB-03]
The antecedent is an alternative representation extension; none is authored. Producing two different record views is not a claim of lossless conversion of arbitrary representations. [10 §§6,8]
There is no newly authored representation-extension mechanism requiring such a data-model mapping. The registry projection is not that mechanism. [10 §§1,6]

DIDP-01 names application/did for its DID1.1 view and DIDP-02/RESOLVE-03 distinguish document media type from the application/json resolution envelope. Frozen DID1.1 §6.3 identifies application/did. This judges selected media identification only, not registration or every implementation convention. [10 §§1,3,5–7]

REG-03/REG-09 specify controller or exact DID/registry/operator/scope authorization, lifecycle eligibility, prior-version comparison and one atomic transition; REG-04 defines proof checks and excludes PoP as authorization. Frozen §7.2 permits out-of-band authority. This closes the abstract permission procedure, not the missing credential/command-binding security contract. [09 §§3,4,6,8,9]

Choose canonical identifier before proofs, reserve unused DID, validate initial record/proofs, bind controller and atomically create version1; chain commit/reveal and web authority are described. Associated created-state projection is explicit. An actual registration or ABI is not inferred. [06 §§1,2,4; 09 §§1,3,4,6,8; 10 §§1,2,6]

DID selects registry/profile; one fresh authorized record is structurally/proof/version checked and projected. Self-validation or explicit authenticated-source trust is stated; web adds exact allowlisted TLS-origin/freshness rules. This is guidance for response authenticity, not a portable proof or completed fork/deployment verification. [09 §§4–6,8; 10 §2]

Key additions/revocations, complete service replacement, lifecycle and scoped-grant changes have explicit eligibility, expected version, immutable fields and atomic record/grant/history effects. The resulting projection is defined. All-command integrity is separately incomplete. [09 §§1,3,9; 10 §§1–3,6]

Authenticated controller or eligible scoped operator can take created/active to terminal deactivated; record remains readable and loses protected usability, with grants removed atomically. This describes how, without certifying live enforcement. [09 §§3,9; 10 §§3,10]
Exactly the case-sensitive did:sage method is defined. Registry kinds are formats inside that one method, not additional method names. [06 §1]

judgments.scope: DID method author; optional path restriction
judgments.review_basis: Closed DID-URL grammar and prose reject paths, exercising the permission to be more restrictive. This does not claim a runtime path-dereference test. [06 §1]

judgments.scope: DID method author; optional query restriction
judgments.review_basis: Closed DID-URL grammar and prose reject queries; no standard optional query support is implied. [06 §1]

judgments.scope: DID method author; optional fragment restriction
judgments.review_basis: key-id is restricted to 1–32 ASCII alphanumeric/hyphen/underscore and a single fragment; absolute full-key references and exact equality are required. [06 §§1,3]

registry-id(kind/locator)+agent-id construction and profile-specific locator lengths/grammars specify the method-specific-id; client chooses agent-id before binding proofs and the registry reserves unused identifiers. [06 §§1,2; 09 §§3,6,8; 11 §5]

Case-sensitive prefix, lowercase kind/chain address, canonical profile form, no percent encoding or aliases and byte-equality semantics are explicit. Noncanonical values are rejected rather than repaired. [06 §§1,2; 09 §§6,8]

The text requires unique registry-id and agent-id, permanent non-reassignment and tombstones; this is useful policy evidence. This statement constrains actual issued values, not merely the author's description. No issuer state/history or independent issuance evidence is in this corpus, so neither runtime PASS nor a collision FAIL is established. [06 §2; 09 §§1,3]

Namespace construction and reservation describe intended global uniqueness under registry/chain trust assumptions. Actual DID issuance and cross-registry/fork deployment behavior were not observed; the separate fork gap is not a demonstrated collision. No issuer result is invented. [06 §2; 09 §§3,5,6]

judgments.scope: DID method author; optional multiple formats
judgments.review_basis: Explicit eip155 and optional web profiles give different fixed locator formats; solana is reserved/rejected rather than an executable third profile. [06 §1; 09 §§6–8; 11 §5]

judgments.scope: DID method author; optional colon syntax
judgments.review_basis: The grammar explicitly partitions registry kind/locator/agent-id with colons and fixes locator segment count by supported profile. No generic meaning for colon is assumed. [06 §1; 09 §6; 11 §5]

Section6.4 addresses all nine RFC6973 §5 categories with public-record/history/query/service consequences and bounded mitigation limits, including intrusion/unsolicited traffic and exclusion. It disclaims erasure, unlinkability and regulatory proof. [06 §6.4; RFC6973 §5]

The obligation is to specify a representation for every abstract-model datatype. SAGE selects existing standard representations and defines closed record projections; it does not author a new representation. Generic producer/consumer completeness is not certified. [10 §§1,6]
No new representation/media-type association is proposed. Using standard application/did in a projection is not authorship of a new IANA representation registration. [10 §§1,6,7]

No new representation-level fragment-processing rules are authored. Method restrictions on full key URLs are distinct from an author defining fragment semantics for a new media type. [06 §§1,3; 10 §4]

No new representation datatype lexical system is defined. Existing standard representations are selected; byte encodings for registry proofs/keys do not redefine DID abstract-model serialization. [10 §§1,6]
The permission to choose alternate lossless datatype serialization is unexercised. Distinct Core1.0/DID1.1 record projections are explicitly not lossless reserialization of one another. [10 §6]
No representation-specific entries-map mechanism is newly defined. The fixed standard context and separate resolution metadata are not a novel mechanism. [10 §§3,6]

judgments.scope: DID method author; composite RFC3552 duty
judgments.review_basis: Residual DoS/exclusions are now substantively discussed, but RFC3552 §5 also requires the authentication method's security assumptions and tight lower-layer protection/combined properties to be specified. Chapter09 still delegates management credential/principal and complete command integrity to unfinished bindings; new6.1/6.2 explicitly acknowledge that gap. Therefore the all-guidelines obligation is still false; this is not inherited solely from its old DoS basis. [06 §§6.1–6.3; 09 §§6,8,9; RFC3552 §5]

judgments.scope: DID method author; cryptographic protection description
judgments.review_basis: The corpus specifies signature domains/covered fields, record PoP, exact HTTP components, complete envelope coverage, HPKE exporter/combiner and session AEAD/AAD, plus channel vs object protection and susceptibility/assumption limits. This is a coverage-description judgment, not proof that every management operation is protected or the composition is secure. [01 §§1–3; 03 §§1–5; 04 §§1–6; 05 §§1–5; 08 §§1–6; 09 §4; 06 §§6.1–6.3]

CRYPTO-05 identifies private/shared/ephemeral and expired traffic secrets and prohibits logging; HPKE names exporter/ack/private state and erasure, session seed/key retention is explicit, and claim salt is secret before reveal. Public keys/records are distinguished. This does not certify custody or erasure implementation. [01 §3; 04 §§2–5; 05 §§1,5; 09 §6; 06 §§6.1,6.4]

judgments.scope: DID method author; conditional document signatures
judgments.review_basis: The DID document is not signed as a whole in this method. Key PoP, signed Agent Cards/messages and authenticated record sources are different objects; no whole-document proof is emitted. The conditional implementation-of-DID-document-signatures recommendation is not exercised. [10 §§1,3,6; 07 §2; 09 §4]

judgments.scope: DID method author; DLT DoS burdens
judgments.review_basis: Section6.3 relates transaction/proof CPU, peer propagation, consensus/finality, storage/history/tombstones and read/RPC burdens to DoS and externalized costs; explains limits of fees and per-record bounds, with measurements still future. The documentary SHOULD does not require invented measured fees. [06 §§6.2,6.3; 09 §§3,5,6]

No DID service type is introduced as a new authentication protocol service. A2AInterface is endpoint eligibility/discovery and grants no authority; existing A2A authentication schemes remain independent. The management proposal is outside this corpus. [09 §1; 11 §8; A2AB-05/06]

judgments.scope: DID method author; all listed attacks
judgments.review_basis: The operation-specific matrix covers eavesdropping, replay, insertion, deletion, modification, DoS, amplification and MITM for creation/mutations/reads. Amplification now includes replication/storage/backend/proof costs. Discussing an acknowledged unmitigated exposure satisfies this discussion duty without claiming all attacks prevented. [06 §6.2]

judgments.scope: DID method author; other known attacks
judgments.review_basis: Registry/key substitution, claim-name racing, stale/rollback source state, parser ambiguity, cross-protocol/key confusion, compromised components and downgrade/bypass are discussed, with charter/integration limits. No completeness or exploit-test claim is inferred. [06 §§3,6.1–6.4; 01; 02 §3; 09 §§4–6; charter §5; EXEC-01/09; A2AB-07]

Compromised controller/trusted source/capture/policy, initially poisoned enrollment, traffic analysis, implementation-boundary failures, finality/outage availability and lack of a forward-secure ratchet are explicit residual risks. Discussion does not repair those exclusions or claim mitigation execution. [06 §§6.1–6.4; charter §5; 04 §6; 05 §5; EXEC-01/09]

judgments.scope: DID method author; all-operation integrity/update authentication
judgments.review_basis: Expected version, immutable fields and atomic grants/history are specified, but no selected binding protects the complete registry/DID/operation/version/arguments association for every management command. PoP/commitment/public-read TLS have narrower coverage. New6.2 records the absence rather than supplying an accepted command encoding/credential integration. [09 §§3,4,6,8,9; 06 §6.2]

Management requires trusted authenticated controller/operator credentials but still leaves their actual method, credential-to-principal association, termination, compromise and replay characteristics to future deployment bindings. Describing trust assumptions generically is not specifying the selected method. The TMP proposal is not normative corpus evidence. [09 §§1,6,8,9; 06 §§6.1,6.2]

judgments.scope: DID method author; assignment policy discussion
judgments.review_basis: Registry-qualified namespace, one registry per registry-id, unique local reservation, immutable/non-reassigned IDs and tombstones are stated, including independent claim races and proof-vs-authorization limits. This discusses policy; actual issuer uniqueness remains NOT_RUN and fork means remain deficient. [06 §§1,2,6.2; 09 §§1,3,6]

Web reads require allowlisted exact HTTPS origin and controlled destinations, no redirects/Card endpoint substitution, explicit authenticated-source trust; application HTTP/Card binding and expected-peer rules are discussed separately. Endpoint discovery is not authority. This does not certify roots/DNS/operations or fill unspecified management authentication. [09 §§5,8; 10 §§2,5; 03 §§2,5; A2AB-05/06; 06 §§6.1,6.2]

judgments.scope: DID method author; topology trust assumptions
judgments.review_basis: The chain profile requires self-validated node or explicitly trusted authenticated resolver and configured readiness/finalized state, rejects arbitrary latest RPC as proof, and distinguishes malicious trusted validators and coherent observations. It does not claim a light-client verifier or all-network topology implementation. Fork selection remains separate. [09 §§5,6; 10 §2; 06 §§6.1,6.3]

judgments.scope: DID method author; optional path/query dereference
judgments.review_basis: SAGE explicitly excludes paths and queries and defines only canonical full-key URL dereference. It therefore does not exercise this permission to supply method path/query processing. This is compatible with the separately exercised narrower-syntax permissions. [06 §1; 10 §4]
No extension specification for DID-path dereferencing is authored. A2A and MCP application bindings are not such DID URL extensions. [06 §1; 10 §4; profile scopes]
No DID-query dereferencing extension is authored; method queries are rejected. [06 §1; 10 §4]

RESOLVE-03 and DIDP-04 emit no equivalentId and define no alternate equivalent forms. The conditional equivalence guarantee is not exercised; ignoring a received alias does not validate that alias. [10 §§3,9]
No canonicalId metadata is emitted and no alias-to-canonical mapping is defined. Canonical syntax of the one id is not a canonicalId assertion. [06 §2; 10 §§3,9]

The DID Resolution interface maps local SAGE diagnostics to existing standard error types and carries sageCode; it does not declare a newly defined DID Resolution error type refining another. Separate SAGE problem URIs do not exercise this refinement declaration. [10 §§5,10]

REG-05/RESOLVE-02 give a self-validating trusted-node route and an explicitly authenticated trusted-source route, with coherent fresh observations, proof validation and rollback/readiness refusal. Frozen §8.1 expressly permits local trusted and remote trusted secure-channel architectures. No trustless portability or runtime availability is claimed. [09 §§4–6,8; 10 §2]

judgments.scope: DID method author; use of declared verification proofs
judgments.review_basis: The method's record proofs have specified exact challenge fields/domains, signer/algorithm checks and verification ordering; RESOLVE-02 requires their verification before projection. Their contribution is record/key binding under authenticated-state assumptions, not proof of finality or a whole returned document to an untrusted client. That use is documented; stronger portable result proofs are not implied. [09 §4; 10 §§1,2; 01 §§1–3]

judgments.scope: DID method author; optional embedded result proofs
judgments.review_basis: No method result/state proof is placed in the DID document or its metadata. Registry PoP and separately signed Cards are not an embedded resolution-proof property. This optional placement is not exercised. [10 §§1,3,6]

judgments.scope: DLT DID method author; fork-disambiguation recommendation
judgments.review_basis: Chain ID, registry address/code, finalized block hash and monotonic versions do not choose or reject competing branches retaining those identifiers. The corpus still leaves the complete branch/consensus/attestation binding unspecified; new6.2 admits this. The separate TMP fork proposal is excluded and cannot close this recommendation. [06 §§2,6.2; 09 §§5,6; 10 §2]

review_policy: fixed independent author judgments on the complete exact corpus; no arbitrary prose classifier
